messages:
alice_sales: FinSight POC hitting streaming disconnects after ~3-5 minutes when traffic goes through their corporate proxy. Node client ok, Python stalls with connection resets. Anyone seen this pattern?

devon_eng: Which Python lib/version? streaming method (chunked) or websockets? any client logs?

alice_sales: Python SDK 0.9.3 async (aiohttp). Server-sent chunked long completions. Error they pasted: 
```
aiohttp.client_exceptions.ServerDisconnectedError: 500, message='Connection lost while reading'
TRACE: HTTP/2 RST_STREAM / GOAWAY
```

zara_infra: BlueCorp proxy we've seen kills idle HTTP/2 streams. Node has different keepalive defaults, so it survives. Python's TCP keepalive often off by default.

tim_sre: Short-term: force HTTP/1.1 or enable socket keepalive and reduce connector pool size. Also bump client stream timeout.

devon_eng: Quick repro config we've used with customers:
Python (aiohttp):
```python
conn = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=1, keepalive_timeout=60)
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=conn)
# set SDK opts: stream_timeout_ms=120000, max_concurrency=1
```
Node (parity):
```js
const agent = new Agent({ connections: 1, keepAliveTimeout: 60000 })
fetch(url, { dispatcher: agent })
```

alice_sales: Customer tried TCPConnector change; drops reduced but still occasional RST. Infra will try increasing proxy idle timer.

zara_infra: If proxy can't be reconfig'd, recommend switching to HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming for stability. Or enable HTTP/2 pings on proxy backend path.

tim_sre: I put a KB note in internal docs: "proxy + streaming: prefer keepalive-enabled connectors and limit connection reuse." Link: https://intra.redwood/KB/proxy-streaming-guidance :thumbsup:

devon_eng: Action items: I'll prepare a one-pager with exact Python/Node snippets plus a checklist (collect GOAWAY/RST timestamps, proxy logs). If they can't change proxy, we advise HTTP/1.1 fallback.

alice_sales: Thanks. Sales note: no pricing change, just POC config ask. Scheduling 30m call with FinSight infra now. Assigning follow-up to @devon_eng.
